senses.en: the ability to understand something immediately without conscious reasoning

ex.en: My intuition told me something was wrong before I opened the door.
ex.zh: 開門之前，我的直覺就告訴我事情不對勁。

senses.en: to overwhelm with a large amount of things
to flood

ex.en: Fans will inundate the website with orders when the tickets go on sale.
ex.zh: 門票一開賣，歌迷的訂單就會湧進網站。

senses.en: a flood; an overwhelming amount of something

ex.en: The inundation of the rice fields ruined the harvest.
ex.zh: 稻田被水淹沒，毀了收成。

senses.en: to make someone used to something unpleasant

ex.en: Years of working in the ER can inure doctors to the sight of blood.
ex.zh: 在急診室工作多年，醫生對血腥場面會變得習以為常。

parts.m: use, work 使用（古法文 euvre）

mn: 常用句型 be inured to：對…習以為常。

senses.en: not legally or officially acceptable
not based on sound reasoning
[ˋɪnvəlɪd] a person weakened by illness or injury

ex.en: Your passport is invalid because it expired last month.
ex.zh: 你的護照上個月到期，已經失效了。

parts.m: strong, worth 有力的、有價值的

root.note: 沒有效力的 → 無效的

mn: 形容詞「無效的」重音在第二音節；名詞「病人」重音在第一音節。

senses.en: to make something legally void
to prove an argument or theory wrong

ex.en: Opening the device yourself will invalidate the warranty.
ex.zh: 自行拆開這個裝置會讓保固失效。

senses.en: extremely useful or valuable

ex.en: Your advice has been invaluable to me during this difficult time.
ex.zh: 在這段艱難時期，你的建議對我來說非常寶貴。

root.note: 價值高到無法估計的 → 無價的

mn: invaluable 不是「沒價值」，而是「價值高到無法估算」；「沒價值」是 valueless。

senses.en: never changing

ex.en: His invariable breakfast is toast and black coffee.
ex.zh: 他的早餐一成不變，總是吐司配黑咖啡。

senses.en: the act of an army entering a country by force
an unwelcome intrusion

ex.en: Reading someone's diary is an invasion of privacy.
ex.zh: 偷看別人的日記是侵犯隱私。

root.note: 走進（別人的地方）→ 入侵

senses.en: insulting, abusive, or highly critical language

ex.en: The online debate quickly turned into a stream of invective.
ex.zh: 網路上的辯論很快就變成一連串的謾罵。

root.note: 把話帶著衝向對方 → 謾罵

senses.en: to speak or write about something with great hostility

ex.en: The critic loves to inveigh against modern architecture.
ex.zh: 那位評論家很喜歡猛烈抨擊現代建築。

root.note: 帶著怒氣衝向對方 → 抨擊

mn: 常與 against 連用：inveigh against；gh 不發音。

senses.en: having or showing creativity and new ideas
senses.zh: 有創意的；有發明才能的

ex.en: The chef is known for her inventive use of local ingredients.
ex.zh: 這位主廚以創意運用在地食材聞名。

root.note: 想法自己冒出來的 → 有創意的

senses.en: opposite in position, direction, or relationship
the exact opposite

ex.en: There is an inverse relationship between price and demand.
ex.zh: 價格和需求之間呈反向關係。

senses.en: the act of turning something upside down or reversing its order
(grammar) reversing the normal word order

ex.en: "Never have I seen such a mess" is an example of inversion.
ex.zh: 「Never have I seen such a mess」是倒裝句的例子。

senses.en: to turn upside down or reverse the order of

ex.en: Carefully invert the cake pan onto a plate.
ex.zh: 小心地把蛋糕模倒扣在盤子上。

senses.en: a person who examines facts to discover the truth

ex.en: An insurance investigator examined the damaged car.
ex.zh: 保險調查員檢查了那輛受損的車。

root.note: 循著足跡追查的人 → 調查員

senses.en: a person or organization that puts money into something to earn a profit

ex.en: The startup found an investor willing to fund its first year.
ex.zh: 這家新創公司找到一位願意資助第一年營運的投資人。

root.note: 把錢「穿」進事業中的人 → 投資人

senses.en: having a long-established habit that is unlikely to change
senses.zh: 根深柢固的；積習難改的

ex.en: My uncle is an inveterate gambler who cannot pass a casino.
ex.zh: 我叔叔是個積習難改的賭徒，經過賭場就忍不住進去。

root.note: 年代久遠的 → 根深柢固的

senses.en: likely to cause resentment or unfairly discriminating

ex.en: The coach was in the invidious position of choosing between two friends.
ex.zh: 教練陷入必須在兩位朋友中二選一、吃力不討好的處境。

root.note: 用嫉妒的眼光看 → 招人嫉恨的

senses.en: to give strength, energy, or life to

ex.en: A cold shower can invigorate you in the morning.
ex.zh: 早上沖個冷水澡能讓你精神一振。

senses.en: too strong to be defeated

ex.en: After ten straight wins, the team seemed invincible.
ex.zh: 連贏十場後，這支球隊似乎所向無敵。

senses.en: never to be broken, attacked, or dishonored

ex.en: The constitution treats freedom of speech as an inviolable right.
ex.zh: 憲法把言論自由視為不可侵犯的權利。

senses.en: to cite or appeal to a law, rule, or authority as support
to call on a god or spirit for help
to bring a feeling or image to mind

ex.en: The witness decided to invoke her right to remain silent.
ex.zh: 證人決定行使她的緘默權。

mn: invoke（援引、祈求）vs. evoke（喚起回憶或感受）。

senses.en: done without conscious control
done against one's will

ex.en: She let out an involuntary gasp when she saw the price.
ex.zh: 她看到價錢時忍不住倒抽一口氣。

root.note: 不是出於意志的 → 不自覺的

senses.en: the process of becoming complicated or intricate
(biology) the shrinking of an organ to its former size

ex.en: The involution of the plot made the novel hard to follow.
ex.zh: 這部小說情節錯綜複雜，很難讀懂。

mn: 中國網路用語「內捲」常譯為 involution。

senses.en: to include something as a necessary part
to cause someone to take part in something

ex.en: The job will involve a lot of travel.
ex.zh: 這份工作需要經常出差。

senses.en: impossible to harm or damage
senses.zh: 刀槍不入的；無懈可擊的

ex.en: No computer system is completely invulnerable to hackers.
ex.zh: 沒有任何電腦系統能完全不受駭客攻擊。

senses.en: privately, in one's mind, without showing it

ex.en: She smiled politely but inwardly groaned at the bad joke.
ex.zh: 她禮貌地微笑，心裡卻對那個爛笑話暗自叫苦。

senses.en: an extremely small amount
the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet

ex.en: There is not one iota of truth in that rumor.
ex.zh: 那則謠言沒有半點真實性。

mn: iota 是希臘字母中最小的一個，所以引申為「一丁點」。

senses.en: easily made angry

ex.en: The irascible old man yelled at anyone who parked near his house.
ex.zh: 那個脾氣暴躁的老人會對任何把車停在他家附近的人大吼。

senses.en: extremely angry

ex.en: Irate passengers crowded the desk after the flight was canceled.
ex.zh: 班機取消後，憤怒的乘客擠滿了櫃台。

senses.en: anger

ex.en: The new parking fees drew the ire of local residents.
ex.zh: 新的停車費引發當地居民的怒火。

mn: 常見說法 draw the ire of：引起…的憤怒。

senses.en: a display of shimmering rainbow colors that change with the angle of view

ex.en: The iridescence of the beetle's shell comes from tiny layered structures.
ex.zh: 這種甲蟲外殼的虹彩來自微小的層狀結構。

root.note: 呈現彩虹般的顏色 → 虹彩

senses.en: showing shimmering colors that change with the angle of view

ex.en: Soap bubbles have an iridescent surface.
ex.zh: 肥皂泡有彩虹般閃爍的表面。

senses.en: to irritate or annoy

ex.en: It will irk her if you are late again.
ex.zh: 如果你又遲到，她會很不高興。

senses.en: annoying or tiresome

ex.en: Filling out the same form three times was irksome.
ex.zh: 同一份表格要填三次真令人厭煩。

senses.en: a situation that is strange or funny because it is the opposite of what is expected
the use of words to express the opposite of their literal meaning

ex.en: The irony is that the fire station burned down.
ex.zh: 諷刺的是，消防局自己被燒毀了。

parts.m: pretended ignorance 假裝無知（希臘文 eirōneia）

root.note: 假裝不懂、說反話 → 反諷

senses.en: (physics) the amount of light energy falling on a surface
(literary) radiance; brightness

ex.en: Solar panels produce more power when irradiance is high.
ex.zh: 輻照度高時，太陽能板的發電量更大。

root.note: 光線照在上面 → 輻照度

senses.en: to expose something to radiation
to light up; to make bright

ex.en: Some companies irradiate food to kill harmful bacteria.
ex.zh: 有些公司用輻射照射食品來殺死有害細菌。

senses.en: not logical or reasonable
(math) not expressible as a ratio of two integers

ex.en: She has an irrational fear of butterflies.
ex.zh: 她莫名其妙地害怕蝴蝶。

senses.en: impossible to reduce or simplify further
senses.zh: 不能再簡化的；不可約的

ex.en: The report cut costs to an irreducible minimum.
ex.zh: 這份報告把成本壓到無法再低的最低限度。

senses.en: impossible to refute or deny
senses.zh: 無可辯駁的；不容置疑的

ex.en: The fingerprints provided irrefragable evidence of his presence.
ex.zh: 指紋提供了他在場的無可辯駁的證據。

senses.en: not to be broken or violated
senses.zh: 不可違背的；牢不可破的

senses.en: (of light) not able to be refracted

ex.en: The monks followed an irrefrangible rule of silence.
ex.zh: 修士們遵守一條不可違背的靜默戒律。

senses.en: not connected with or important to the matter

ex.en: Your age is irrelevant to whether you can join the club.
ex.zh: 你的年齡和你能不能加入社團無關。

root.note: 不能拿來支撐論點的 → 不相干的

senses.en: not religious; hostile to or indifferent to religion
senses.zh: 無宗教信仰的；反宗教的

ex.en: Though raised in an irreligious home, she later became a nun.
ex.zh: 雖然她在沒有宗教信仰的家庭長大，後來卻成了修女。

senses.en: impossible to repair or put right
senses.zh: 無法修復的；不可挽回的

ex.en: The flood caused irreparable damage to the old library.
ex.zh: 洪水對那座老圖書館造成無法挽回的損害。

senses.en: not able to be controlled or held back, usually in a cheerful way
senses.zh: 抑制不住的；活力十足的

ex.en: Her irrepressible enthusiasm made everyone want to join the project.
ex.zh: 她那壓抑不住的熱情讓大家都想加入這個計畫。

senses.en: too attractive or strong to be resisted

ex.en: The smell of fresh bread was irresistible.
ex.zh: 剛出爐麵包的香味讓人無法抗拒。

root.note: 無法站著對抗的 → 無法抗拒的

senses.en: not showing proper care for the consequences of one's actions

ex.en: It is irresponsible to text while driving.
ex.zh: 開車時傳簡訊是不負責任的行為。

root.note: 無法回應承諾的 → 不負責任的

senses.en: a lack of respect for people or things usually taken seriously

ex.en: The comedian is famous for his irreverence toward politicians.
ex.zh: 這位喜劇演員以對政客毫不客氣聞名。

senses.en: showing a lack of respect, often in a humorous way

ex.en: The magazine is known for its irreverent humor.
ex.zh: 這本雜誌以玩世不恭的幽默著稱。

senses.en: (rare) showing a lack of reverence; irreverent

ex.en: His irreverential remarks at the ceremony offended the elders.
ex.zh: 他在典禮上不敬的言論冒犯了長輩們。

senses.en: impossible to change back to a previous state

ex.en: Some effects of climate change may already be irreversible.
ex.zh: 氣候變遷的某些影響可能已經無法逆轉。

senses.en: (medicine) a liquid used to wash out a wound or body cavity

ex.en: The dentist used a saline irrigant to clean the tooth.
ex.zh: 牙醫用食鹽水沖洗液清潔那顆牙齒。

senses.en: to supply water to land or crops through channels or pipes
(medicine) to wash out a wound with a flow of liquid

ex.en: Farmers use river water to irrigate their fields.
ex.zh: 農民利用河水灌溉田地。

senses.en: easily annoyed or made angry
(of a body part) overly sensitive
senses.zh: （身體部位）過敏的；易受刺激的

ex.en: Lack of sleep makes me irritable in the morning.
ex.zh: 睡眠不足讓我早上很煩躁。

senses.en: the quality of causing irritation or annoyance

ex.en: Scientists tested the skin irritancy of the new soap.
ex.zh: 科學家測試了新肥皂對皮膚的刺激性。

senses.en: a substance that causes slight swelling or discomfort
something that continually annoys

ex.en: Smoke is a common irritant for people with asthma.
ex.zh: 煙對氣喘患者來說是常見的刺激物。

senses.en: to make someone annoyed or angry
to cause soreness or discomfort to part of the body

ex.en: Wool sweaters often irritate my skin.
ex.zh: 羊毛衣常會刺激我的皮膚。

senses.en: a sudden, violent entry; a sudden increase in an animal population

ex.en: Birdwatchers were thrilled by the irruption of snowy owls this winter.
ex.zh: 今年冬天雪鴞數量暴增，讓賞鳥人士興奮不已。

mn: irruption 是「衝進來」；eruption 是「爆發出去」。

senses.en: (literary) an island, especially a small one

ex.en: They spent their honeymoon on a quiet isle in the Mediterranean.
ex.zh: 他們在地中海一座寧靜的小島上度蜜月。

mn: s 不發音，和 aisle（走道）同音。

senses.en: a very small island

ex.en: Seabirds nest on a rocky islet just off the coast.
ex.zh: 海鳥在海岸外一座岩石小島上築巢。

senses.en: a line on a weather map connecting places with the same air pressure

ex.en: On a weather map, each isobar connects places with equal air pressure.
ex.zh: 在天氣圖上，每一條等壓線都連接氣壓相等的地點。

senses.en: occurring at equal intervals of time

ex.en: A pendulum's swings are nearly isochronous, which makes it useful in clocks.
ex.zh: 鐘擺的擺動幾乎是等時的，所以適合用在時鐘上。

senses.en: to separate someone or something from others
to identify and separate out a substance or cause

ex.en: Doctors had to isolate the patient to stop the infection from spreading.
ex.zh: 醫生必須隔離病人，以防感染擴散。

senses.en: having or taking place at a constant temperature

ex.en: In an isothermal process, the gas stays at the same temperature.
ex.zh: 在等溫過程中，氣體保持相同溫度。

senses.en: traveling from place to place, especially for work
a person who travels from place to place

ex.en: The itinerant musician played in a different town every night.
ex.zh: 那位流浪樂手每晚都在不同的小鎮演出。

root.note: 一直在旅途中的 → 巡迴的

senses.en: a planned route or schedule for a trip

ex.en: Our itinerary includes three days in Kyoto and two in Osaka.
ex.zh: 我們的行程包括在京都三天、大阪兩天。

senses.en: to travel from place to place, especially to preach or work

ex.en: In the 1800s, many preachers would itinerate through frontier towns.
ex.zh: 在 19 世紀，許多傳教士會在邊疆小鎮之間巡迴佈道。

senses.en: special words used by a particular group that others find hard to understand

ex.en: The lawyer explained the contract without using legal jargon.
ex.zh: 律師不用法律術語，把合約解釋得很清楚。

senses.en: a medical condition that makes the skin and eyes turn yellow
bitterness or resentful cynicism

ex.en: The newborn baby was treated for mild jaundice.
ex.zh: 那個新生兒接受了輕微黃疸的治療。

root.note: 皮膚變黃的病 → 黃疸

mn: 形容詞 jaundiced 常指「帶有偏見、憤世嫉俗的」，如 a jaundiced view。

senses.en: to put something at risk of being harmed or lost

ex.en: One careless mistake could jeopardize the whole mission.
ex.zh: 一個粗心的錯誤就可能危及整個任務。

parts.m: even game, risk 勝負未定的賭局（古法文 jeu parti）

root.note: 勝負未定、置於風險中 → 危及

senses.en: a person who supports an aggressive, warlike foreign policy; an extreme patriot
senses.zh: 好戰的愛國主義者；沙文主義者

senses.en: (by jingo) an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise

ex.en: Every jingo in parliament cheered for war.
ex.zh: 國會裡每個好戰的沙文主義者都為開戰喝采。

mn: 源自 19 世紀英國的愛國歌曲「We don't want to fight, but by Jingo if we do」，衍生 jingoism（好戰愛國主義）。

senses.en: playful or humorous

ex.en: His jocose manner put the nervous guests at ease.
ex.zh: 他詼諧的態度讓緊張的客人放鬆下來。

root.note: 充滿玩笑的 → 詼諧的

senses.en: fond of joking; humorous

ex.en: The principal gave a jocular speech that made the students laugh.
ex.zh: 校長發表了一場幽默的演講，逗得學生哈哈大笑。

senses.en: to shake or move with small, quick jerks
a slight shake or jolt

ex.en: Try not to joggle the table while I'm pouring the tea.
ex.zh: 我倒茶的時候盡量別晃到桌子。
